transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
I came in because I’m just so tired. I can barely make it through a shift at work. It feels like my whole body is filled with wet sand, and even when I rest, I don’t really feel better.
Have you been feeling down or depressed?
I don’t know if I’d call it depressed exactly. I’m just really worn out and not feeling like myself. It’s been hard to keep going like normal.
When you sleep, do you wake up feeling refreshed?

No, not really. With my shifts changing around, I got to where I’d only sleep a few hours and still feel kind of wired. And now, even when I’m really exhausted, I wake up early and my mind is already going.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah. Things I usually like just don’t really do much for me right now. I used to cook for myself, play guitar, go hiking, visit my family… and now it all just feels kind of flat, like I’m going through the motions or pretending I care.
Have you been feeling sad or low most days?
I’m not sure I’d say sad most days. It’s more like I feel low and kind of empty a lot of the time, but I haven’t really been tracking it day by day.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

Yeah, definitely. At work especially, when I’m ringing people up, every little thing pulls me off track — the scanner beeping, construction noise from the remodel, somebody walking past. I’ll just lose track of what I was doing.
Have you been having thoughts that life isn’t worth living?

Yeah… I have. I’ve had thoughts like maybe everyone would be better off if I just didn’t wake up. And a few times, walking home, I caught myself thinking about just stepping off the curb into traffic. It scares me.
For the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day nearly every day?
I’m not really sure. I know I’ve felt low a lot, but I haven’t been keeping track of whether it’s most of the day every day.
Lately, have you been feeling sad or depressed?
I guess… yeah, I’ve been feeling pretty sad lately. Not all the time maybe, but enough that I notice it.
During the past two weeks, have you felt sad or down nearly every day?
I don’t know if I can say nearly every day. I’ve felt down a lot, but I haven’t really been keeping track day by day.
Have you had a period where you felt unusually energized or high?

Yeah. There was a stretch where I felt really energized, like almost unstoppable, and I was in a really good mood. But I’d also get irritated fast, like snapping over little things, even something like being asked to count a drawer again.
During that energized stretch, did you need much less sleep than usual?

Yeah, I did. With my shifts changing around, I got to where I’d only sleep a few hours and still feel wired, like I didn’t need more. And now even when I’m exhausted, I wake up early and my mind is already going.
During that energized stretch, were you more active than usual or taking on more projects?

Yeah, definitely. At work I started volunteering for extra cash-office stuff, and I’d be reorganizing shelves even when nobody asked me to. I had this whole idea for a promotion binder I was putting together. Then I’d go home and still feel like doing more, like shopping online or rearranging my apartment.
During that energized stretch, did you feel unusually confident or like you could do things other people couldn’t?

I don’t know if I’d say I felt like I could do things other people couldn’t. I felt more sure of myself, maybe, but not like I had some special ability or anything. Just more confident than usual, I guess.
About how long did that energized stretch last?
It’s been about a month, I think. It started around when the store changed our hours for the remodel, and it’s kind of just kept going since then.
During that energized stretch, did it cause serious problems in your life or at work?

Yeah, it did. At work I started making mistakes on the register and falling behind on the cash-office stuff, and my manager actually took me off some responsibilities I was hoping would help me get promoted. That was embarrassing.

And outside of work, I’ve been avoiding my family more. It got bad enough that I needed same-day crisis help because I didn’t feel safe handling it by myself.
During that energized stretch, were you talking more than usual or so fast that other people noticed?

Yeah. People at work kept telling me to slow down. I’d be talking really fast about the schedule, inventory stuff, or ideas I had for being a supervisor, and I could tell they weren’t really keeping up with me.
During that energized stretch, did you feel unusually important or powerful?
I don’t know if I’d say powerful. I mean, I felt more confident than usual, like I could handle more than I probably could, but I’m not sure it was like feeling unusually important.
During that energized stretch, were you more active than usual or taking on more projects?

Yeah, definitely. I was taking on way more than I usually would. I volunteered for extra cash-office work, started reorganizing shelves, and I was making this whole binder with ideas for promotions. Then I’d go home and still feel like doing more, like shopping online or rearranging my apartment.
During that energized stretch, did you do anything unusually risky or impulsive?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I did more shopping than usual and made quick decisions, but I don’t know if I’d call it risky. Nothing really stands out to me beyond being more impulsive with little stuff.
